title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from this and the neighbouring pages). Over some base, Grothendieck has flat group schemes B'_0 (rel. dim 2), T_rho (2), N'_sigma (2) and G (4), and SG (3). The dimensions suggest G = GL_2 and SG = SL_2, but this is not certain. He forms G*_{rho,sigma} ≅ B'_0 × T_rho × N'_sigma and the semidirect product S~M_{rho,sigma} = G*_{rho,sigma} · G. In it, G*_{rho,sigma} acts on G by inner automorphisms through the factor B'_0, which maps into G. The canonical maps of the four factors into the semidirect product are called i_B, i_rho, i_sigma, i_G. A subgroup L_0 ≅ G_m of B'_0 gives the 'principal monomorphism' i : L_0 → S~M_{rho,sigma}, λ ↦ (λ,1,1,λ^{-1}) = i_B(λ) i_G(λ^{-1}) (written τ(λ) once on this page). On the previous page he worried that it is not clear this image is normal in the larger group S~M (as opposed to SM). This page checks normality on the four kinds of generators, using T-valued points.
(1) i_rho(x), i_sigma(x): T_rho and N'_sigma commute with B'_0 and act trivially on G, so they centralize i(L_0).
(2) x ∈ B'_0:
  i_B(x) i(λ) i_B(x)^{-1} = i_B(xλx^{-1}) · i_G(xλ^{-1}x^{-1}) = i(x(λ)),
  where x(λ) = xλx^{-1}. This tacitly needs L_0 to be stable under conjugation by B'_0. Phrased differently: i : L_0 → G*·G is B'_0-equivariant for the natural actions on the two sides, the action on the target being via i_B.
(3) x ∈ G: by definition i_B(λ) and i_G(λ) act on G in the same way, so i(λ) = i_B(λ) i_G(λ)^{-1} centralizes G. Hence i_G(x) i(λ) i_G(x)^{-1} = i(λ). The marginal note says to state at the outset that i(λ) commutes with G.
Conclusion: i(L_0) ≅ G_m is a normal subgroup scheme. On the next page he divides by it to get groups M_{rho,sigma} and M~_{rho,sigma} of relative dimension 6 and 9. These sit in a diagram of central-type extensions by G_m (43) and are identified with semidirect products G*(0)·G and SG*(0)·SG (44). The underlying algebra is the standard fact that H ⋉_φ G, with H acting through a homomorphism φ: H → G by inner automorphisms, is isomorphic to H × G via (h,g) ↦ (h, φ(h)g). Under this isomorphism the 'anti-diagonal' {(h, φ(h)^{-1})} is the factor H × 1, so any subgroup of it coming from a normal subgroup of H is normal.
errors: Gap: the B'_0 step needs x(λ) = xλx^{-1} to lie in L_0, i.e. L_0 must be normal (e.g. central) in B'_0. This is not stated on the page. It is automatic if B'_0 is commutative, e.g. a torus.
Notation slip: τ(λ) is used once for i(λ).

In the B'_0 computation the intermediate term i_G(x)(i_G(λ^{-1})) is silently substituted for i_B(x)(i_G(λ^{-1})). This is correct only because B'_0 acts on G through i_G∘(B'_0 → G), which is precisely the defining convention.

ideas.what: In a semidirect product where the acting group acts by inner automorphisms through a homomorphism to G, the anti-diagonal elements i_B(λ)i_G(λ)^{-1} centralize G and form a normal subgroup; quotienting by a G_m of such elements yields the group M_{rho,sigma}
ideas.modern_name: untwisting an inner semidirect product (H ⋉ G ≅ H × G); quotient by a normal/central anti-diagonal subgroup, as in GL_2 ×_{G_m} ... constructions

ideas.what: Construction of flat group schemes M_{rho,sigma}, M~_{rho,sigma} (relative dimension 6 and 9) as quotients by G_m, within the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' programme
ideas.modern_name: auxiliary algebraic symmetry groups for the loop/Galois equations (precise modern counterpart unclear)
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to themes of La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981); unsure

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine verification that a G_m 'anti-diagonal' subgroup is normal in a semidirect product. It is needed to pass to a quotient group scheme on the next page. The algebra is standard; it has one small unstated hypothesis (L_0 stable under B'_0) and no new idea.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 more likely reads 'Il est entendu, bien sûr, que l'on fait opérer G*_{rho,sigma} sur G intérieurement via le facteur B'_0'; the '∫' is a misreading of 'on fait'.

The line rendered 'ce qui montre que L_0 \ G*·G = S~G* commute : l'action naturelle de B'_0 sur les deux noyaux' should probably read 'ce qui montre que L_0 --i--> G*_{rho,sigma}·G = S~M_{rho,sigma} commute à l'action naturelle de B'_0 sur les deux membres (sur le deuxième via i_B : B'_0 → S~M_{rho,sigma})'.
The marginal note should probably read 'dire tout de suite que i(λ) commute à G, donc i(λ) opère trivialement sur G!'; 'i_rho' there is a misreading.
In the underbrace, i_B(x(λ)): the crossed-out text is a false start, giving i_B(x(λ)).
'peut se rentrer sous le facteur' is likely 'peut se mettre avant/sous le facteur i(λ)'; the meaning is that i_G(x)^{-1} commutes past i(λ).
